# 8599 - TRI-STATE 64-bit RAM (16 x 4), outputs inverted

Package DIP-16 · family 8000 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/8599.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/8599.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 51 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![8599 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/8599.png) | ![8599 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-8599.png) | ![8599 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-8599.png) |

A rectangle for the whole function (or one section of it). Pin numbers are written on the lines where they meet the box; signal names are written beside them.

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

## Pins

| Pin | Name | Role | Active | Output type | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A0 | input |  |  |  |
| 2 | ME | enable | low |  | controls pins 5, 7, 9, 11; when not enabled: float |
| 3 | WE | input | low |  |  |
| 4 | D1 | input |  |  |  |
| 5 | S1 | output |  | three-state | enabled by ME |
| 6 | D2 | input |  |  |  |
| 7 | S2 | output |  | three-state | enabled by ME |
| 8 | GND | ground |  |  |  |
| 9 | S3 | output |  | three-state | enabled by ME |
| 10 | D3 | input |  |  |  |
| 11 | S4 | output |  | three-state | enabled by ME |
| 12 | D4 | input |  |  |  |
| 13 | A3 | input |  |  |  |
| 14 | A2 | input |  |  |  |
| 15 | A1 | input |  |  |  |
| 16 | VCC | power |  |  | +5 V |

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 5,7,9,11 | Sn = NOT mem[A3..A0][n] when ME' AND WE; Z when ME high | With ME low and WE high, S1..S4 show the COMPLEMENT of the 4-bit word stored at address A3..A0. With ME high the outputs float. |

## Stored state

Bits stored: 64

Changes on: level: ME low and WE low

- ME L, WE L: D1..D4 written into word A3..A0
- ME L, WE H: read, outputs show the complement of the stored word
- ME H: hold, outputs Hi-Z

|---|---|

## Not known

- The truth table gives the outputs during a write only as part of the "complement of data" column header; the write-cycle waveform was not read.
- Which edge of WE the setup/hold times refer to was not read from the waveform.

## Notes

Same pinout as 7489, with three-state outputs.

## Sources

- [National Semiconductor 1976 TTL Databook, DM75/DM8599 TRI-STATE 64-Bit Random Access Memories](https://www.bitsavers.org/components/national/_dataBooks/1976_National_TTL_Databook.pdf) - pdf 472-475 (printed 3-127..3-130); DM8599
